# Results — Study 803 (Realized-Skewness Reversal)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Amaya,
Christoffersen, Jacobs & Vasquez (2015): stocks with high **realized skewness** earn
**lower** future returns, so a long-low-skew / short-high-skew book should earn a positive
spread. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current
month is dropped). Fingerprint `5384b8f7f128` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-21-day realized skewness** of daily simple returns (population third standardised moment, vectorised via `m3 / m2**1.5`), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the bottom 30%** (low skew), **short the top 30%** (high skew), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled low-vs-high books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Crucially,
the realized-skewness premium is documented as a **small-and-illiquid-stock** effect; a
50-mega-cap survivor panel is exactly where it is *least* likely to appear — which is what we
find.

## The headline — long-low-skew / short-high-skew spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% minus top-30% realized-skew spread (n = **4,125** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long low-skew − short high-skew)** | **−3.19 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−3.04** |
| one-sample *t* | −2.98 |
| low-skew book / high-skew book | +6.15 bps / +9.34 bps (Welch *t* = −1.25) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.74 |

The claimed edge **fails to replicate — and inverts.** Amaya et al predict a *positive*
long-low/short-high spread (low-skew names out-earn); on this mega-cap universe the spread is
**significantly negative** (−3.19 bps/day, NW *t* = −3.04): the lottery-like **high-skew**
names actually *out-earned* the boring low-skew ones over 2010–2026 (these are the momentum
tech mega-caps whose right tails paid off). The realized-skewness premium is an
illiquid-stock phenomenon that does not survive on 50 mega-caps.

## Placebo — is the (reversed) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-skew sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−3.19 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.005 bps (0.873) |
| position of observed | ≈ **3.65σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 1.000 ⇒ left-tail p ≈ 0.000) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −3.19 bps sits far in the **left** tail, so
the (opposite-sign) relation is real and not a lucky sort — the sign is simply the reverse of
the literature's on this universe.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,991) | −2.37 bps | **−2.12** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −3.95 bps | **−2.27** |

The reversal holds in both halves — this is not one era's artefact.

## The timer — can you get paid for it (even the reversed book)?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −3.19 bps | 2.14 bps | **−5.33 bps** | −4.98 | −1.23 | −13.4%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −3.19 bps | 10.14 bps | **−13.33 bps** | −12.46 | −3.08 | −33.6%/yr |

The specified book loses money gross; and even the *sign-flipped* book (long high-skew) would
earn only +3.19 bps/day gross, which the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a mere 1 bp
one-way already eats most of, dying entirely at any realistic cost. **Mirage** either way.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "skew tilt" that shapes each name's return
skewness and (with `edge>0`) depresses its forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.22** (sd 0.96), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0016`, seed 803) | **+7.70** (Welch *t* = +7.71) |

The detector recovers a *planted* Amaya relation cleanly and never fires on the null — so the
negative real-tape result is a genuine sign-reversal on the mega-cap universe, not a bug.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The famous Amaya-et-al negative realized-skewness premium does **not**
  replicate on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-low-skew / short-high-skew spread is
  **−3.19 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−3.04**) — significant but *opposite in sign* to the claim,
  holding in both eras (*t* = −2.12 / −2.27), ≈3.65σ into the left tail of a 1,000-permutation
  placebo, with a clean 20-seed synthetic control. The claimed edge is absent (the effect is an
  illiquid-stock phenomenon); on mega-caps the lottery names out-earned.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified book loses money gross and net (−5.33 bps/day at 1 bp,
  −13.33 at 5 bps); even the data-mined sign-flip is eaten by the round-trip friction at 1 bp.
